templates.title: The lamps in the Barrow
templates.premise: Someone has lit the old lamps. No one living holds the key.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 put out the lamps one by one, and at the last lamp said the old words. The Barrow is dark again, as it should be.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 put the lamps out. Whoever lit them did not come to stop it.
endings.SETBACK: %1 reached the third lamp before the rest went out on their own. Something was walking in the dark.
endings.DISASTER: The lamps went out all at once. %1 had to find the door by touch.

templates.title: A name scratched out
templates.premise: A grave marker has been defaced. The dead man walks at night, looking for who did it.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 found the name in the parish book and cut it back into the stone, deeper than before. He lay down at dawn.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 found the name and cut it back into the stone. He has not walked since.
endings.SETBACK: %1 cut a name into the stone. It was the wrong name. He was not grateful.
endings.DISASTER: The dead man decided it was %1 who had done it.

templates.title: The Barrow-king wakes
templates.premise: The door of the deepest mound stands open from within.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 met the Barrow-king on his own stair and sent him back down it. The door is shut and the stone rolled over.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 held the stair until sunrise. The king went back to his bed.
endings.SETBACK: %1 held the stair for an hour. It was not long enough, but it was long enough to get out.
endings.DISASTER: The Barrow-king came up the stair faster than anything dead should move. %1 broke and ran.

templates.title: Grave goods
templates.premise: Robbers went in at dusk. Bring them out, or what is left.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 brought out all four robbers alive, and every ring they had taken went back on its finger.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 brought the robbers out. They were glad to be arrested.
endings.SETBACK: %1 found the robbers' lantern and one boot. Then the passage came down.
endings.DISASTER: The robbers had woken what they came to rob. %1 walked into the middle of it.

templates.title: The bell under the tide
templates.premise: A church bell rings from under the water at low tide.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 waded out at the ebb and rang the bell back. It tolled once in answer and has been silent since.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 said the office for the drowned parish from the shore. The bell stopped before the end.
endings.SETBACK: %1 stayed too long listening. The tide came in behind.
endings.DISASTER: The bell was calling, and %1 answered. The sea closed over the sandbar.

templates.title: The wreck of the Heron
templates.premise: A ship has broken on the Teeth. There may be living aboard.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 rowed out four times and brought back eleven living, and the ship's cat.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 got a line to the wreck. Six came down it before the hull went.
endings.SETBACK: The boat turned over in the surf. %1 came ashore, but no one from the Heron did.
endings.DISASTER: The Teeth took the boat as they had taken the ship. %1 went into the water a mile from shore.

templates.title: What the nets raised
templates.premise: The fishers will not go out until it is dealt with.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 killed it on the shingle and burned it above the tide line. The boats went out the next morning.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 drove it back into deep water. The fishers mend their nets and do not speak of it.
endings.SETBACK: It took the net, the winch, and part of the jetty, with %1 standing on it.
endings.DISASTER: It came up the beach after %1. No one had known it could leave the water.

templates.title: The tide tables
templates.premise: The sea is keeping a different calendar. Someone must learn it.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 watched a month of tides and wrote the new tables out fair. The harbormaster wept.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 worked out the new tides, near enough. The boats sail by it.
endings.SETBACK: %1 trusted the third night's reckoning, and was cut off on the causeway until morning.
endings.DISASTER: The tide that caught %1 was in no table, old or new.

templates.title: The rope bridge
templates.premise: The bridge at Hollow Gap is down, and a caravan is on the wrong side.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 carried the first line across hand over hand, and had mules crossing by evening.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 strung a new bridge. It sways, but it holds.
endings.SETBACK: The anchor post pulled free. %1 hung over the Gap a long while before anyone could haul.
endings.DISASTER: The rope parted over the middle of the Gap, with %1 on it.

templates.title: The hermit's fire
templates.premise: No smoke from the high cell in nine days.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 found the hermit alive, snow-blind and singing, and carried him down on a door.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 relit the fire and left wood for a month. The hermit did not say thank you. He has a vow.
endings.SETBACK: The hermit had been dead a week. %1 buried him in a storm and came down frostbitten.
endings.DISASTER: The storm shut the path behind %1. There was no wood in the cell.

templates.title: First snow
templates.premise: The shepherds are late down the mountain.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 found the shepherds and every sheep, and brought them down by a path nobody knew was there.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 brought the shepherds down. Half the flock followed.
endings.SETBACK: %1 found the shepherds, then lost the path. Two nights in a snow hole.
endings.DISASTER: The slope let go above %1. It was very quiet after.

templates.title: The horn in the ice
templates.premise: A war-horn sounds each night from inside the glacier.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 cut down to the horn-blower and told him the war was over, and who had won. He put down the horn.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 sat a night by the ice and answered every call. At dawn the horn sounded the stand-down.
endings.SETBACK: %1 answered the horn wrongly. The ice cracked from one side of the valley to the other.
endings.DISASTER: The horn was a summons. %1 heard an army get to its feet under the ice.

templates.title: The unquiet forge
templates.premise: The smiths have fled their own forge. It burns without them.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 worked the bellows until the fire had made what it wanted to make, and then it slept.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 banked the forge with wet sand and patience. The smiths have come back.
endings.SETBACK: %1 got the doors shut. The roof did not wait.
endings.DISASTER: The forge was not empty. %1 opened the doors and the fire walked out.

templates.title: Ash on the orchards
templates.premise: The mountain is breathing. Get the villages out.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 had three villages on the road by noon, with their pigs and their grandmothers. Nobody was left.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 emptied the villages in time. The orchards are gone.
endings.SETBACK: One farm would not leave. %1 went back for them through the ashfall.
endings.DISASTER: The mountain did not wait for %1 to finish counting heads.

templates.title: The fire-walker
templates.premise: She will quiet the vents, for a riddle answered.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 answered her riddle and asked one back. She is still thinking. The vents are quiet.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 answered well enough. She quieted the vents and kept the change.
endings.SETBACK: %1 answered wrongly. She let it pass, but the walk back was across the coals.
endings.DISASTER: She does not like a careless answer. %1 gave one.

templates.title: A light in the caldera
templates.premise: Something is building a nest of coals.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 broke the nest and quenched the clutch. One cold egg came home as a paperweight.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 scattered the nest. Whatever built it has gone deeper.
endings.SETBACK: The builder came home with %1 still in the nest.
endings.DISASTER: The clutch had hatched. %1 met them on the caldera wall.

templates.title: The long feast
templates.premise: The King is counting his friends.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 sat below the salt, and by the third course had been moved above it. The King remembers the house.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 ate what was served and laughed at the right jokes. The house is counted a friend.
endings.SETBACK: %1 laughed at the wrong joke. There was a duel in the yard afterward.
endings.DISASTER: The feast was a net. Before it ended %1 had been named in a quarrel that was waiting for a name.

templates.title: The petition
templates.premise: Forty villages, one hearing. Speak well.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 spoke for an hour without notes. The tax is lifted, and the clerks stood up when it was done.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 spoke, and the Court listened. The tax is halved.
endings.SETBACK: %1 spoke well, and then the chancellor spoke. The villages' friends were followed home.
endings.DISASTER: %1 said the true thing in the wrong room. The guard was called.

templates.title: The tourney
templates.premise: Lances at noon, before the whole Court.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 unhorsed the King's champion and handed him back his helm. The crowd has not stopped talking.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 rode three courses and kept the saddle. Honor is satisfied.
endings.SETBACK: %1 took a lance in the shoulder in front of four thousand people.
endings.DISASTER: The champion's lance was not blunted. %1 learned it at the gallop.

templates.title: Knives at the masque
templates.premise: Someone means to kill the chancellor in a crowded hall.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 found the knife before it was drawn, and the hand, and the purse that paid the hand.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 stood in the way. The chancellor lives and the music did not stop.
endings.SETBACK: %1 stopped the knife the hard way.
endings.DISASTER: There were three knives. %1 had counted one.

templates.title: The boar of Harrow Dell
templates.premise: It has taken three hunters. It is not an ordinary boar.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 took the boar at the ford, on foot. Its tusks hang over the hearth now.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 drove the boar over the ridge. Harrow Dell can gather wood again.
endings.SETBACK: The boar doubled back. %1 spent the night in a tree, bleeding.
endings.DISASTER: The boar had been hunting %1 since the tree line.

templates.title: The charcoal road
templates.premise: Two went in after berries. Bring lanterns.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 found both children asleep in a badger sett, and carried them out singing so they would not be afraid.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 found the children by their crying. Both are home.
endings.SETBACK: %1 found one child. The search for the other went on in the dark, and went badly.
endings.DISASTER: The lanterns went out a mile in. %1 called, and something that was not a child called back.

templates.title: Wolves keeping sheep
templates.premise: A flock, fenced and tended, and no shepherd in sight.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 worked out who the wolves were working for, and bought the contract.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 watched three nights and came home with an answer nobody likes. The flock is left alone.
endings.SETBACK: %1 stepped over the fence to count the sheep. The wolves take that seriously.
endings.DISASTER: The flock was bait. %1 understood it from inside the fence.

templates.title: The heart of the wood
templates.premise: No one has been that far and said what was there.

endings.TRIUMPH: %1 reached the heart of the wood, and came back, and will say only that it was kind.
endings.SUCCESS: %1 went as far as the standing stone and left the offering. The wood gave a clear road home.
endings.SETBACK: The paths moved. %1 walked nine days to cover three miles.
endings.DISASTER: %1 reached the heart of the wood. It had been waiting a long time for company.
